items.title: 6.5 Enthalpy change of reaction and chemical bonds

source_refs.note: Topic 6.5, printed page 123; Sample Problem 6.1. The print's 'Figure 6.5' reference is to the bond-energy illustration, carried by the Hess and bonds original.

blocks.text: A chemical reaction is a process in which old bonds are broken and new bonds are formed, so the enthalpy change of a reaction comes from the breaking and forming of chemical bonds. A chemical bond is a form of energy, chemical energy, interconvertible with all other forms. Bond breaking absorbs energy (delta H positive) and bond formation releases it (delta H negative), and their difference decides the overall sign: a reaction is exothermic if the energy released in making new bonds exceeds that absorbed in breaking old ones, and endothermic otherwise. In the formation of water, energy is needed to break the H-H bonds and the O=O bonds while energy is released in making the H-O bonds, and the net reaction is exothermic because more is released than absorbed: 2H2(g) + O2(g) gives 2H2O(g), delta Hr negative.
